translationRepairs: Liang then advised Xiang Liang: 'You have already established the Chu successor, but among the Han princes Lord Hengyang Cheng Xian can be established as king, to further build alliances.'
Liang then advised Xiang Liang: 'You have already established the Chu successor, but among the Han princes Lord Hengyang, Cheng, is worthy and can be established as king, to further build alliances.'
橫陽君成賢 takes 成 as the given name and 賢 as the predicate worthy, not a name Cheng Xian. The following unit seeks 韓成, confirming that parsing. The replacement is accurate.

He appointed Liang as Han envoy, with the King of Han leading over a thousand men raiding Han territory to the west, capturing several cities, but Qin always recaptured them, going back and forth as roaming troops in Yingchuan.

He appointed Liang as Han Minister over the Masses, and with the King of Han they led over a thousand men raiding Han territory to the west, capturing several cities, but Qin always recaptured them, going back and forth as roaming troops in Yingchuan.
韓申徒 is the Han office equivalent to 司徒, not envoy, and 與韓王將 means Liang and the King of Han jointly led the troops, not that the king alone led.

Liang once idly strolled leisurely on the bridge at Xiapi, when an old man in coarse clothing came to where Liang was, directly dropped his shoe down into the bridge, turned and told Liang: 'Young man, go down and get my shoe!'

Liang once idly strolled leisurely on the bridge at Xiapi, when an old man in coarse clothing came to where Liang was, deliberately dropped his shoe off the bridge, turned and told Liang: 'Young man, go down and get my shoe!'
直墮其履圯下 means the shoe was dropped below the bridge, not into the bridge; 直 here marks a deliberate drop. The replacement corrects that spatial error.
Pursued north to Lantian, fought again, Qin troops utterly defeated.
He pursued the routed enemy to Lantian, fought again, and the Qin troops were utterly defeated.
（遂）［逐］北 means pursuing a routed force (北 as 敗北), not traveling north, and the silent subject continues 沛公 from the previous sentence.
Thus, reached Xianyang, Qin prince Zi Ying surrendered to Duke Pei.
Thus they reached Xianyang, and Ziying, King of Qin, surrendered to Duke Pei.
秦王子嬰 is Ziying, King of Qin: 王 is king, not prince, and 子嬰 is one personal name, not Zi Ying.
They pressed on to Xianyang, where Ziying, the last King of Qin, surrendered to the Duke of Pei.
They pressed on to Xianyang, where Ziying, King of Qin, surrendered to the Duke of Pei.
The Chinese names him 秦王子嬰 and does not call him the last king. Last is an inserted gloss not present in this sentence.

When they reached Xiayi, the King of Han dismounted and sat upon his saddle, asking, 'I would give up everything east of the passes. Who among the lords is worthy enough to share the task of defeating Chu?'
When they reached Xiayi, the King of Han dismounted and sat upon his saddle, asking, 'I would give up everything east of the passes. Who can share the achievement with me?'
誰可與共功者 asks who can share the deed or merit. Among the lords and the task of defeating Chu are not in this sentence and invent referents.
The King of Han answered, "I cannot."
The silent-subject reply 曰：「未能也。」 continues the King of Han in this Han-year-3 exchange addressed as 陛下; calling him emperor is anachronistic.
The King of Han answered, "I cannot."
The silent-subject reply 曰：「未能也。」 continues the King of Han in this Han-year-3 exchange addressed as 陛下; calling him emperor is anachronistic.
When King Wu entered Yin, he honored Shang Rong's gate, released jizi's imprisonment, sealed Bi Gan's grave.
When King Wu entered Yin, he honored Shang Rong's gate, released Jizi from imprisonment, and raised a mound over Bigan's grave.
箕子 is the name Jizi; 釋箕子之拘 is release from confinement, not released imprisonment; 封比干之墓 honors the grave with a mound rather than sealing it.

固陵 is the place Guling, already used in the idiomatic rendering. Gulang is a wrong reading of the same toponym.

The emperor wished to depose the crown prince, establish Lady Qi's son King Zhao of You.
The emperor wished to depose the crown prince and establish Lady Qi's son Ruyi, King of Zhao.
趙王如意 is Ruyi, King of Zhao. King Zhao of You reverses the title 趙王 and the given name 如意.

The ministers around him were all Shandong people, many advised the emperor to establish capital in Luoyang: 'Luoyang east has Chenggao, west has Xiaomeng, with the Yellow River behind, facing Yi and Luo—its fortifications are also sufficient to rely on.'

The ministers around him were all Shandong people, many advised the emperor to establish the capital in Luoyang: 'Luoyang east has Chenggao, west has Xiao and Mian, with the Yellow River behind, facing Yi and Luo—its fortifications are also sufficient to rely on.'
殽黽 are the Xiao and Mian passes, not a single invented place Xiaomeng. The replacement restores the two names.

Guanzhong has Xiao to the left, Han to the right, fertile plains a thousand li, south has Bashu's wealth, north has the Xiongnu's advantages, blocking three sides to defend, alone using one side east to control the feudal lords.

Guanzhong has Xiao and Hangu to the left, Long and Shu to the right, fertile plains a thousand li, south has Ba-Shu's wealth, north has the advantage of the Hu pasturelands, blocking three sides to defend, alone using one side east to control the feudal lords.
左殽函 is Xiao and Hangu, not Han; 右隴蜀 is Long and Shu; 胡苑之利 is the advantage of Hu pasturelands, not specifically the Xiongnu.
Thus, the emperor set up wine, enfeoffed Yong Chi as Marquis of Shifang, and urgently urged the chancellor and superintendent to determine merits and carry out enfeoffments.
Thus, the emperor set up wine, enfeoffed Yong Chi as Marquis of Shifang, and urgently urged the chancellor and the imperial secretary to determine merits and carry out enfeoffments.
御史 is the imperial secretary, not a generic superintendent. The proposed office is right, but the parenthetical pinyin gloss is unnecessary in the English sentence.

Your servant has heard 'a mother who loves her child embraces him', now Lady Qi serves day and night, King Zhao You Yi is constantly held in front, the emperor says 'I will never let an unworthy son be placed above a beloved son', clearly his replacing the crown prince's position is certain.

Your servant has heard 'a mother who loves her child embraces him'; now Lady Qi serves day and night, Ruyi, King of Zhao, is constantly held in front; the emperor says 'I will never let an unworthy son be placed above a beloved son'; clearly his replacing the crown prince's position is certain.
趙王如意 is Ruyi, King of Zhao, not King Zhao You Yi. The replacement restores the title and given name.
Gaozu departed from difficulties several times, yet the Marquis of Liu constantly had meritorious strength—how can this not be called heaven?
Gaozu encountered difficulties several times, yet the Marquis of Liu constantly had meritorious strength—how can this not be called Heaven?
高祖離困者數矣 uses 離 as 罹, to meet with hardship, not to depart from difficulties. The replacement restores that sense.
I considered this person in planning to be stalwart and extraordinary, until seeing his portrait, his appearance was like a woman or beautiful girl.
I had supposed this man to be stalwart and extraordinary, until seeing his portrait; his appearance was like that of a woman or a beautiful girl.
其人計魁梧奇偉 uses 計 as the historian’s supposition about Zhang Liang’s physique, not in planning.
